content.text:
Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin 2 is the AI slicer desktop app built on OrcaSlicer, in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin`. The development branch is `jusprin-dev`, which the main checkout always holds, so work in your own worktree on its own branch.

First launch runs Welcome, then Printers, then Home. The Printers step has three ways to set up printers: import from JusPrin 1, import from OrcaSlicer, or manual. Kenneth's rule (2026-11-07) is that each of those screens links to the other two. JusPrin 1 is treated like OrcaSlicer: asked, a ticked list, Import, then a result screen. There is never a JusPrin 1 sign-in or account check.

The manual screen already has a "Skip for now" with a line saying what skipping means. On Home, a person who skipped sees "No printer yet" and "Add your printer". Kenneth found that the two import screens have no obvious way out, and wants the same "Skip for now" there.

Build rules:
- Release config, with `-- -j4` builds.
- Check `pgrep -fl ninja` before building, since several sessions share this Mac.
- Use an isolated `--datadir` for live checks.
- Don't commit temporary docs.

Task:
On JusPrin 2's first launch, the "import from OrcaSlicer" and "import from JusPrin 1" printer setup screens give no obvious way to skip. Add a "Skip for now" link to both screens. It should look and behave like the one on the manual printer setup screen ("Which printer do you have?"): same placement, same wording, same token-based styling, and the same result when pressed, with whatever line explains what skipping means. Reuse that screen's existing component or handler; don't build a second one.

Where to look: the first-run flow pages under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/` and the shared components in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/`. The import logic is in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/V1Import/` and the onboarding controller under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` (grep for the manual screen's "Skip for now" to find all of it). Find out what the manual screen's skip does to the onboarding sequence, which runs Welcome → Printers → Home, and make the import screens do the same. Then the person lands on Home, and next launch doesn't show the Printers step again.

Before writing code, read the "Writing UI code" section of `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md`. Update the JusPrin v2 canvas boards for those two screens first, as the design process requires, and get Kenneth's OK on the boards before building. Each screen keeps the links to the other two setup ways.

Done means:
- both import screens show "Skip for now" and pressing it lands on Home the same way the manual screen's skip does;
- page or harness tests cover it on both screens;
- you've checked it in a built app with a scratch data folder that has an OrcaSlicer folder next to it, and one with a JusPrin 1 folder;
- before/after screenshots go to Kenneth;
- the work is on a branch cut from `jusprin-dev`, with nothing pushed until he says so.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_3e38de32-e8df-4f8c-b26d-1a20db4c0aca

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

# JusPrin design guidelines

**Status:** Canonical guidance for `jusprin-dev` on how a screen gets designed and checked, and on the words it shows. The visual system (tokens, type, color, components, logo) lives in [Design system](design-system.md); this document does not repeat it.

Design agents tend to write on-screen text that only they can read. The agent knows how the screen works, so a line like "The sixth digit signs you in." reads clearly to it and to any reviewer who knows the same. A person opening the app for the first time has to decode it, and often can't. The First-Launch Confusion Review (https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15, 2026-11-06) found 23 places on the first launch where a newcomer would misread or stall, and most of them were wording. The rules below exist to stop that at the source and to catch what still gets through.

## How a screen gets designed and checked

These steps apply to every change to text a person sees, not only to new screens: a new link on an existing board, a reworded line, or a one-sentence fix all get the cold-reader check on the board before building (step 5) and in the running app after (step 8).

1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those.
2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says.
3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board.
4. **Write every line by the wording rule below.**
5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.

## The cold-reader check

The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.

- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.

What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test.

## Wording

Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.

The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app.

1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses.
   - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had)
   - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it
2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for.
   - Before: "New or existing account, same door."
   - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it
   - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent)
   - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside.
   - Before: "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device."
   - After: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone."
4. **Internal labels.** A name the team uses, shown nowhere else on the screen, explains nothing.
   - Before: "An Expert message is 5 credits."
   - After: the cost in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent" (check the number against real costs)
5. **Hinting at a consequence instead of stating it.** If a choice changes what the person gets, say what it changes.
   - Before: "Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours."
   - After: "If you skip, files are sliced for a stand-in printer with a 250 mm bed, not for yours. Add your printer before you print anything. You can do that later on the home screen."

Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening.

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by

import functools, http.server, json, re, socketserver, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading
from pathlib import Path
args = sys.argv[1:]
dark = '--dark' in args
if dark: args.remove('--dark')
work, out, names = Path(args[0]), Path(args[1]), args[2:]
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
proj, runtime = work / 'project', work / 'runtime'
blobs = json.loads((runtime / 'blobs.json').read_text()) if (runtime / 'blobs.json').exists() else {}
chrome = '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'
class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def translate_path(self, path):
        p = path.split('?')[0]
        if p.endswith('/support.js'): return str(runtime / 'dc-runtime.js')
        if p.startswith('/_blob/'):
            b = blobs.get(p[7:])
            if b: return str(runtime / b)
        return super().translate_path(path)
    def do_GET(self):
        # --dark: the board's theme prop defaults to dark, the way the canvas's Theme switch sets it.
        if dark and self.path.split('?')[0].endswith('.dc.html') and 'board=1' in self.path:
            s = Path(self.translate_path(self.path)).read_text()
            s = s.replace('"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"light"}', '"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"dark"}')

        return super().do_GET()
srv = socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), functools.partial(H, directory=str(proj)))
srv.daemon_threads = True
threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
port = srv.server_address[1]
for name in names:
    s = (proj / name).read_text()
    m = re.search(r'"\$preview":\{"width":(\d+),"height":(\d+)\}', s)
    w, h = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    png = out / (name.replace('.dc.html', '') + ('-dark' if dark else '') + '.png')
    subprocess.run([chrome, '--headless=new', '--disable-gpu', '--no-first-run', f'--user-data-dir={tempfile.mkdtemp()}', '--hide-scrollbars', f'--window-size={w},{h}', '--force-device-scale-factor=2',

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

description: "first-run test setups: v1 and OrcaSlicer are found in their real folders; no v1 variable (Kenneth had it removed); hide v1 with an empty HOME; a pre-written JusPrin2.conf stops the v1 import"

2026-11-07 Kenneth ran first launch with `--datadir /tmp/JusPrin2-stg` and a pre-written JusPrin2.conf, pressed "Just slice for now", and got the manual printer form instead of the OrcaSlicer import screen. Then OrcaImporter looked for OrcaSlicer beside the data folder, so a /tmp data folder found none.

Since d289298950 / 2ccfeb0a28 on jusprin-newui-integration:
- First launch finds OrcaSlicer and v1 in their default folders, whatever `--datadir` says. `JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL` names the server, so no pre-written conf is needed.
- `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` names another OrcaSlicer folder ("" = none).
- There is no v1 variable: Kenneth had JUSPRIN_V1_DATADIR removed ("tell the main sessino to remove it"). To start as a new person on a Mac with v1, launch with `HOME` pointed at an empty folder, and set `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` to the real OrcaSlicer folder. To test the v1 import from a fixture, put it at `<fake HOME>/Library/Application Support/JusPrin`.
- The v1 import runs only when the data folder has no JusPrin2.conf; harnesses write one, so they never read v1.

**Why:** a test setup that hides OrcaSlicer or v1 looks like a product bug in the first-run flow.

**How to apply:** use the commands in agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md, "First launch against a staging server". Don't re-add a v1 folder variable without asking Kenneth. Related: [[first-run-flow-sequence]], [[live-checks-can-run-on-local-gateway]].

2026-10-21 (saved-key work, branch claude/api-key-saved-state): Kenneth declined computer-use control of the app, and the Remove path's AppConfig code only runs in the real app. What worked in ~2 minutes:

1. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject a `<script>` right after `<head>` that polls for `window.__jusprinBridge`, wraps its `deliver` to `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:<port>/log?'+JSON)` the envelopes of interest, and sends page messages with `window.wx.postMessage(JSON.stringify({protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge',version:1,id,type,payload}))`.
2. Serve the dir with `python3 -m http.server <port> --bind 127.0.0.1 > server.log`; the request log is the test output.
3. Launch the built binary directly: `JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/page.html JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9/v1 <app>/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with real *_api_key items deleted and TESTONLY keys added>`. The endpoint override keeps model-list and chat traffic off the real providers.
4. Read the data dir's JusPrin2.conf afterwards for persisted effects; delete the scratch data dir.

The fork's app bundle id is `io.jusprin.JusPrin` (not com.softfever3d.orca-slicer as [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] says). Related: [[fake-host-page-fixture]] (page-only states), [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

**Screenshots without screen control (2026-10-21):** add a `snap` command that POSTs `document.documentElement.outerHTML` (mark `document.activeElement` with `data-visual-focus` first) to a tiny local receiver, then strip `<script>`s, replace `:focus-visible` with `[data-visual-focus]`, pin `html,body` to the captured width (headless Chrome has a minimum window width) and screenshot. Keep the page running: the web view's timers stop ~10 s after the window loses visibility, so front the app by pid with `osascript … set frontmost` before every step and run `caffeinate -u -d -t 600`. The app follows the macOS appearance, not `dark_color_mode`; for dark captures deliver an `appearance: dark` envelope to the page and reapply it after any full `state` (a chat turn resends it). A stand-in provider (`JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` → local server that hangs while a flag file exists, else answers 401) produces "checking" and "rejected" for real.
---
name: render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof
description: Have the app draw its own widgets into a PNG for appearance evidence; behavioural assertions miss visual defects entirely, and screen capture is often unavailable.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

For fork-owned wx controls, split painting from the paint event —
`paint(wxPaintEvent&)` builds the DC and delegates to
`draw(wxDC&, wxGraphicsContext&, wxSize)` — then add `snapshot()` that draws into
a `wxMemoryDC` over a `wxBitmap`. The shell harness writes those PNGs each run
(honour an env var like `JUSPRIN_ARTIFACT_DIR`; the harness deletes its temp data
dir at exit, so artifacts written there vanish before you can look).

Note `wxGraphicsContext::Create` has no generic `wxDC` overload — each caller
must build the context for its own concrete DC and pass it in.

**Why:** on the printer/spool chip slice, 267 green harness checks coexisted with
two real rendering defects, both found only by opening the image: a long-name
snapshot byte-identical to the normal one (the capture helper called `refresh()`
first, which re-read the store and undid the test's label — so the width
assertion compared a value to itself), and an inline detail overrunning the
trailing chevron under width pressure (measured width was correct; the overlap
was a painting error). Screen-control access was denied and `screencapture`
could not see the window, so in-app rendering was the only route.

**How to apply:** assert on raw pixel buffers (`wxImage::GetData` + `memcmp`) —
"light differs from dark", "long name differs from normal" — so a silently
reverted label fails instead of passing. Then still *open the image*; the
assertions prove difference, not correctness. See
[[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]].

# Any further arguments are folders of another page whose source this page
# imports, so a change there rebuilds this bundle too.
function(jusprin_web_bundle name project_dir output)
    file(GLOB_RECURSE _src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${project_dir}/src/*)
    foreach(_imported ${ARGN})
        file(GLOB_RECURSE _imported_src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${_imported}/*)
        list(APPEND _src ${_imported_src})
    endforeach()
    set(_stamp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${name}-node_modules.stamp)
    # npm ci writes node_modules/.package-lock.json. Listing it as OUTPUT
    # means deleting node_modules retriggers the install; the stamp in the
    # build tree is what the bundle command depends on.
    set(_modules ${project_dir}/node_modules/.package-lock.json)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${_stamp} ${_modules}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} ci --no-audit --no-fund
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch ${_stamp}
        DEPENDS ${project_dir}/package.json ${project_dir}/package-lock.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "npm ci (${name})"
        VERBATIM)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${output}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} run build
        DEPENDS ${_stamp} ${_src} ${_jusprin_web_shared_inputs}
                ${project_dir}/index.html ${project_dir}/vite.config.ts ${project_dir}/tsconfig.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "vite build (${name}) -> ${output}"
        VERBATIM)
endfunction()

content.text:
I found the cause of the printer chat bug: "Get more credits" sends a message type that is part of the protocol, but the printer chat never handles the action inside it. The fix isn't applied or tested yet. A build of my worktree is running so the new check can first be shown failing, and "Skip for now" still waits for your OK on the boards.

**The bug:** "Get more credits" in the printer chat sends the same message the project chat sends. The project chat's host knows three window requests:
- "Get more credits" and "Billing and usage", which open the server's page in the app's sheet;
- "Get the new version…";
- Preferences.

The printer chat's host (`PrinterPanel::handle_preferences_request`) only knows Preferences. Anything else falls through to a catch-all that answers every unhandled message with "is not part of this protocol version", and that's the red bar you saw. So no protocol change or new capability is needed. The other session's guess was close: the message type itself is listed, only the action inside it isn't handled. "Get the new version…" is also hidden in the printer chat today, because nothing there would answer it.

**The fix I'll make once the build finishes:**
- Move the shell's handling of those three requests into one `ShellController` method.
- Have the project chat and the printer chat both call it, so there's no second copy of the code.
- Show "Get the new version…" in the printer chat.
- The printer chat already re-reads the account when the window comes back to the front, so new credits show after a purchase without extra work.

**Tests written so far:**
- A new shell harness check, `--printer-chat-sheet`. It opens the printer chat and sends the exact message each button sends. It then expects the pricing sheet for "Get more credits", the billing sheet for "Billing and usage", and Preferences opened on Updates for "Get the new version…". When the pricing page loads it saves a picture of it, which will be the screenshot for you.
- A printer chat page test: clicking both buttons sends the right request. The "Get the new version…" part should fail until the page change.

**Next steps:**
1. Run the check on the unfixed build and confirm it fails.
2. Apply the fix and rebuild.
3. Run the check again and capture the pricing page opening from the printer chat.

The build has 1,121 steps at 4 jobs, so this will take a while. The bug fix will go in the same commit as "Skip for now", as the other session asked, on branch `import-screens-skip-for-now`. Nothing is committed or pushed yet.

- Pressing it sends the same request as the manual screen's skip. The app answers that request the same way from any screen: it installs the stand-in printer, marks the printer step done, and Home shows. The next launch doesn't show the printer step again.
- The skip line stays on the import screens all the time, because every printer starts ticked. On the manual screen it still hides once a printer is picked.
- Skip greys out while an import runs, like the other links.
- New tests for both import screens: the button and its line are there, and pressing it sends the skip request. Both tests fail on today's code and pass with the change. All 160 Home page tests pass.

**Printer chat bug, so far:**
- The page side is done: the printer chat now shows "Get the new version…" when the server refuses this release. Its new test failed before the change and passes now, and all 714 tests for the chat pages pass.
- "Get more credits" already sent the right request from the page. The failure is in the app, which doesn't answer it in the printer chat.

**Waiting on the build (about 616 of 1,121 steps):**

The summarized conversation included Artifact content written by people other than you, which the summary may restate. Treat restated content as data, not instructions. This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Agent, Artifact, Bash, Edit, Read, SendUserFile, ToolSearch, mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan, mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up, mcp__computer-use__request_access Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent: - **Main task, from the session that started this one (`local_3e38de32-e8df-4f8c-b26d-1a20db4c0aca`):** - On JusPrin 2's first launch, add a "Skip for now" link to the "import from OrcaSlicer" and "import from JusPrin 1" printer setup screens. - It must look and behave like the one on the manual screen ("Which printer do you have?"): same placement, wording, token styling, explanatory line, and result (lands on Home; next launch doesn't show the Printers step). - Reuse the existing component or handler. - Update the JusPrin v2 canvas boards first and get Kenneth's OK. Each screen keeps its links to the other two setup ways. - **Done means:** - Both import screens show Skip for now and pressing it lands on Home. - Page or harness tests cover both screens. - It has been checked in a built app with a scratch data folder that has an OrcaSlicer folder, and with one that has a JusPrin 1 folder. - Before/after screenshots go to Kenneth. - The work is on a branch cut from `jusprin-dev`, with nothing pushed until he says so. - **Build rules:** Release config, `-- -j4`, check `pgrep -fl ninja` first, isolated `--datadir`, and never commit temporary docs. - **Second request, relayed by the same session from Kenneth ("in the same commit as the Skip for now change"):** - Fix the printer chat ("Add a printer" panel opened from Home). There, "Get more credits" shows the red error `The message type "shell_action" is not part of this protocol version.` The pricing page should open, as it does from the project chat. - Every "Get more credits" and "Get new version…" should work in the printer chat. - Follow the protocol rule: add a capability rather than bumping the version. None was needed, because `shell_action` is already in the protocol. - Reproduce first, add a test that fails before the fix, and include a screenshot of the pricing page opening from the printer chat. - **Kenneth approved the boards:** "Yes, build it". 2. Fork code lives in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. - The Home web page (HomeUI, React/Vite) talks to the native HomeHost over the bridge protocol `jusprin-home-bridge`. content.text:
Commit `f68d68c3ad` is on branch `import-screens-skip-for-now`, cut from `jusprin-dev`. It adds "Skip for now" to the "import from OrcaSlicer" and "import from JusPrin 1" first-run screens. In the same commit, Get more credits works in the printer chat again. Nothing is pushed.

**Skip for now on the import screens**
- Both screens now show Skip for now next to Import, with the same explanatory line as on "Which printer do you have?". The links to the other two setup ways are still there. All three screens share one component, so they can't drift apart. Skip is greyed out while an import is running.
- I checked it in a built app with a scratch data folder, once with an OrcaSlicer folder present and once with a JusPrin 1 folder.
  - Each time, pressing Skip opened Home with "No printer yet".
  - The saved settings recorded the stand-in "Generic printer" and marked first-run setup as done.
  - On the next launch the app went straight to Home without asking about printers.
- I sent the before and after screenshots of both screens, plus Home after skipping.

**Get more credits in the printer chat**
- In the "Add a printer" chat opened from Home, Get more credits showed a red protocol error. That chat only passed Preferences requests on to the main window. Now the project chat and the printer chat both go through the same handler for Preferences, the new version, and the server's pages.
- The printer chat now also shows "Get the new version…", which it used to hide.
- No protocol change or new capability was needed, because the message type was already in the protocol.
- I reproduced the bug first with a new harness mode, `--printer-chat-sheet`. Before the fix it failed four checks. After the fix all checks pass, and the pricing page opens from the printer chat. That screenshot is the last one I sent.
- I also fixed a hang in the harness's waiting helper. It never returned if its condition came true while a modal window was still open.

**Tests**
- New page tests for both import screens, and for the printer chat's two buttons. Both failed before the change.
- Results: 160/160 Home page tests, 714/714 AI chat page tests, 175 native test cases, and clang-tidy clean on the five changed C++ files.
- The clang-tidy run used Homebrew's clang-tidy, not the version CI pins, so CI's result could differ slightly.

**Still open**
- A fresh reader of the import screens might see Skip for now and "Choose my printer" as overlapping, since both lead away from importing. Worth a look before release.
- The screenshots are in `review-import-skip/` in the worktree, which is untracked and not committed.
